newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SOCCER-AUSTRALIA BEAT NEW ZEALAND TO WIN OCEANIA FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AUSTRALIA BEAT NEW ZEALAND TO WIN OCEANIA FINAL.

text.p: Australia beat New Zealand 2-0 in the second leg of the Oceania qualifying final on Sunday to move a step closer to winning a place in next year's World Cup finals in France.

Ned Zelic opened the scoring with a superb long-range strike in the sixth minute and Graham Arnold sealed victory with a goal in the 53rd minute to give Australia a 5-0 aggregate win following their 3-0 success in last weekend's first leg in Auckland.
The Socceroos will now play the team which finishes fourth in the Asian zone preliminary tournament in a home-and-away series, with the winner qualifying for France.

Sunday's win maintained Australia's perfect record under new coach Terry Venables who was appointed to help the Socceroos reach the World Cup finals for only the second time after their previous appearance in 1974.
Australia have now won 11 matches in succession under Venables and the former England manager said he was delighted with their progress although they had squandered a number of scoring opportunities.
"If I wanted to be super critical then, yes, we can still improve on that," Venables said.
"But I'm well pleased overall. If someone offered me two victories and five goals to nil in these matches before they started, I would have snapped their hands off and taken it."
The match had originally been scheduled to be played at the Sydney Football Stadium on Saturday but was postponed because of a waterlogged pitch and rescheduled for Parramatta Stadium on Sunday.
